primitives.name: Defensive Performance Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: Which defenses had the shortest rest times before they had to re-take the field since 2015?

primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship between rest time and defensive performance holds within 5–20 min range.

The core mathematical structure revolves around modeling defensive rest as a temporal stochastic process. The primitive 'temporal_defensive_rest_duration' defines \( \Delta t_{\text{rest}} \) as a sum of time intervals between defensive snaps, enabling probabilistic characterization of rest patterns. The regression primitive 'defensive_performance_regression' attempts to link \( \Delta t_{\text{rest}} \) to defensive performance metrics, yet empirical findings show near-zero correlation, indicating no statistically significant predictive power. The proxy primitive 'play_based_rest_proxy' acknowledges limitations in direct measurement, substituting time of possession for actual rest time—a substitution that introduces systematic bias. Dualities emerge in the form of temporal vs. play-based proxies, with the former offering precision and the latter accessibility. Failure modes include clock errors and game delays, which corrupt the temporal signal and necessitate data cleaning protocols. The kernel-based approach in GSI leverages these primitives to construct a Bayesian framework for defensive forecasting, while GSE employs them in a Markovian state transition model to simulate situational readiness.
